issues.description: The template's Stock and StockIngredient classes are inconsistent: Stock.java calls stockIngredient.getQuantity(), but the template StockIngredient.java defines retrieveQuantity() instead of getQuantity(). This leads to a compile-time error and contradicts the problem statement instruction to "add getters for all the private fields." The solution repository uses getQuantity(), showing the intended API. Students will be blocked by this naming mismatch when trying to compile and implement the SealSaloon functionality.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the getter name consistent across files. Rename retrieveQuantity() in the template's StockIngredient.java to getQuantity(), or update Stock.java to call retrieveQuantity(). Prefer renaming to getQuantity() to match the problem statement's expectation and the solution implementation so students have a coherent API to use.

issues.description: The template implementation of StockIngredient exposes the ingredient quantity via a method named retrieveQuantity(), while the problem statement (which asks for getters for private fields) and the solution use the conventional name getQuantity(). This naming mismatch breaks the conceptual mapping: students reading the problem expect standard getters (getQuantity) and the Stock class in the template calls getQuantity(), but the template StockIngredient provides retrieveQuantity() instead. This will confuse students and cause compilation/runtime errors when Stock or other classes attempt to call getQuantity().
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity(), or add a getQuantity() method that delegates to retrieveQuantity(), so that StockIngredient provides the expected getter name used by Stock and as required by the problem statement.
